_README: Acknowledged drift for the per-subsystem security audits, checked by
frontend/scripts/check-audit-freshness.mjs (runs in `npm run check`).
An audit's `Audited commit` is the code state its claims were verified
against. When the content under that audit's `Code paths` moves away from
it, the check goes red. Two ways out, both legitimate:
1. Re-verify the audit -> bump `Audited commit` in the doc, add a change
log entry, and drop the audit's entry from this file.
2. Review the drift and conclude it cannot move a verdict -> record the
current object id of each `Code paths` entry in `reviewedTrees`, and
append a dated record to `acknowledgements` saying why.
What is NOT legitimate is recording an object id without reading the diff.
The record is the evidence that someone did.
`reviewedTrees` holds git object ids (a tree for a directory, a blob for a
file), not commit SHAs. Get them from the check itself: when it fails it
prints the current id of every path that moved, ready to paste.
Object ids rather than commit SHAs because this repo squash-merges: a commit
SHA written during a PR stops existing when the PR lands, which used to cost
a follow-up commit per acknowledgement. Squashing rewrites history, not
content, so an object id survives it, along with rebases, cherry-picks and
force pushes.
A path whose every changed file differs from the reviewed state only in
comments and layout has not drifted and needs no entry here. Java,
TypeScript, JavaScript and .properties are read by
frontend/scripts/lib/comment-only.mjs; everything else is compared byte for
byte. The recorded id does not move with such a change, so the next real
change is diffed against the state that was reviewed.
`acknowledgements` is an ordered list of `{ date, note }`, oldest first, and
it is what bounds route 2. Option 2 used to be unbounded: one note string
that only ever grew, so the honest way out stayed available forever and the
audit itself was never read again. Two caps now end that run and force
route 1, whichever comes first:
- 8 acknowledgements. Each one judges its own delta in isolation; the
union of eight of them is not something a ninth reviewer can hold in
their head, and it is the union that decides whether a verdict moved.
- 90 days from the OLDEST record. Drift acknowledged in spring is being
defended by a judgement nobody has revisited.
Both clocks reset the same way: re-verify the audit, bump `Audited commit`,
and delete the entry from this file.

acknowledgements.note: ContactController's GET /autocomplete calls ContactAutocompleteService instead of ContactService, and takes it as one more constructor argument. The service is new in feature/contact/service and holds ContactService's autocomplete and its ranking helpers, moved without change except that the contact half now names the shared order as ContactService.DEFAULT_SORT. The endpoint's mapping, its parameters and their constraints (@Positive accountId, @Size(min = 1) q, @Min(1) limit), ensureContactQueryWithinLimit, the clamp of limit to contactAutocompleteMaxLimit and the response type are byte-identical; no endpoint, request field, response field, validation rule or error path moved, and nothing else in the directory changed. Section 2 holds: the query bound and the limit clamp it cites are the controller's, and the merge bound it names ContactService for stays in ContactService. Verdict unchanged.

The forwarder's Shift branch of the preventDefault predicate grows from /^[rg]$/i to /^[rgi]$/i, so Ctrl+Shift+I (the app's new go-to-Inbox shortcut in globalShortcuts.ts) is cancelled in the frame as Ctrl+Shift+R and Ctrl+Shift+G are; the rest of the script is byte-identical, and the comment above it names the new key. MAIL_FRAME_SCRIPT_SHA256 was recomputed independently (SHA-256 of the string literal, base64: yOywlma3ATltbXiySWrZF0tBX1RtZ0aZRF07BflnLk0=) and matches the constant and mailFrame.test.ts. Section 1 holds: the frame is still sandbox=allow-scripts without allow-same-origin, the CSP still admits exactly that one hash-pinned script, the forwarder still relays only isTrusted keystrokes and anchor clicks and posts the same fields; cancelling one more chord adds no capability and no data to what it sends. The styles, the sanitizer and the other Code paths are untouched. Verdict unchanged.

The only change under message-detail is the remote-image banner in MessageContent.svelte, for testers who could not tell what it was for: its text moves from a muted span to a paragraph that says why the images are held back (the message holds images from the internet that were not loaded, and loading them can tell the sender it was opened), and the i18n strings behind it, the region name and both announcements say 'images from the internet' instead of 'remote images'; the second button is now named 'Always load images from this sender'. The banner is still shown only while renderAsHtml, the count is non-zero and loadRemoteImages is false; the two buttons call the same revealRemoteImages and trustSender, which still send the same allow-list PUT; loadRemoteImages is still seeded per stableId from remoteImagesAllowedForSender; the iframe's sandbox, srcdoc, CSP and the mailFrame message handling are byte-identical. Section 1's tracking-pixel claim holds: no path loads a remote image without one of the two presses. The 2026-07-08 finding record still quotes the button's old English label, which is that date's record and not a claim about the current text. Verdict unchanged.

Audit 2.2. mailFrame.ts: the forwarder cancels one more chord, Ctrl+Shift+W (the Shift list /^[rgi]$/ becomes /^[rgiw]$/), which the app now claims to move focus to the blocked-images banner; MAIL_FRAME_SCRIPT_SHA256 is recomputed from the literal and mailFrame.test.ts asserts it. The CSP directives, the sandbox, the style hashes, the link and height relays and the promote/count functions are untouched. message-detail: MessageContent.svelte takes remoteImageTrustOffered and renders the second button only when it is true and there is an account and an address to key the trust on (the branch that loaded once without remembering is gone with the button), names the address in the button and the announcement, sends the allow-list PUT through mail/remoteImageTrust.ts, which then drops that sender’s cached bodies, and publishes revealRemoteImages and a focus call for the palette command and the shortcut while the banner is shown and the copy is not the print sheet’s. Where the body takes focus on a deliberate open it also pushes one sentence to the polite announcer if the banner is shown; that call writes text to the app’s live region and loads nothing. MessagePrintSheet.svelte passes the new prop. loadRemoteImages is still seeded per stableId from remoteImagesAllowedForSender and set only by revealRemoteImages; the new callers reach that same function, so §2’s tracking-pixel claim holds: no remote image loads without a gesture on that message or a sender the user trusted, and now never by trust alone in junk. Verdict unchanged.

WCAG 2.2 AA fixes. message-detail: MessageHeaderCard.svelte adds `underline` to the class of the sender's "Upravit kontakt" / "Přidat do kontaktů" link and a comment on why (WCAG 1.4.1). The link's href, its accessible name and the rest of the header are unchanged; nothing in the directory that sanitizes, frames, sizes or loads mail content moved, and mailFrame.ts is untouched. Verdict unchanged.

The sign-in-again error names the account. ImapConnectionManager#requireUsableAccount reads the account's e-mail address with the requires_reauth flag in one query (AccountRepository#findEmailIfRequiresReauth, replacing isRequiresReauth) and passes it as {0} of error.mail.accountRequiresReauth; the English fallback message, which is what the log gets, names the account id only. The guard still runs first in executeWithLock and executeWithLockOrSkip, refuses the same accounts with the same code and status, and opens no connection; nothing else in the package moved. Verdict unchanged.

The conversation view moves out of MailFacade into a new ConversationViewService in the same package: getConversations, getThread, crossFolderConversationSizes, conversationExcludedFolders, ConversationScope, conversationScope, threadResponse, folderScopedUnread, scopeToConversationView, survivesCollapse, conversationMemberIdentity and CONVERSATION_EXCLUDED_ROLES. Compared with the old MailFacade text, the code is identical with whitespace ignored; only two javadoc references changed, {@link #getEmails} to MailFacade#getEmails and 'this class' to MailFacade. The new service takes five of MailFacade's collaborators (MessageRepository, MessageMapper, MailSyncService, ImapFolderService, AccountService) and no new one, and is not @Transactional, as the two methods were not. MailFacade.getConversations and getThread keep their signatures and return what the service builds, so MailReadController, the lazy fetch, the listing depth (B1-9) and every role lookup the audit cites are unchanged; the audit names MailFacade only for prepareReply, getEmails, listDrafts and getMessageContentOnly, none of which moved. Nothing else in the package changed. Verdict unchanged.

#932. SmtpMessageService.sendDraftAsync refuses an untouched draft in two places: the server no longer holds it (DRAFT_NOT_FOUND_ON_SERVER, audit reason draft_not_found_on_server) and its copy names other recipients than expectedRecipients (DRAFT_CHANGED_ON_SERVER, draft_changed_on_server, the B1-5 check). Each wrote the audit line, updateLastError and the failed SSE notification inline; both now call one private refuseDraftSend with their code, audit reason and detail, which runs the same three statements in the same order and builds the same strings. Each branch keeps its own log.warn, sets outcome to FAILURE before the call and returns after it. The helper catches nothing, so a failure to persist last_error still falls to the method's catch and is reported as DRAFT_SEND_FAILED, as before. recipientsDiffer, expectedRecipients, the bounded fetch (B1-18), the transport and the draft left in place on a refusal are untouched, so §4e's account of the refusal holds word for word. Nothing else in the package changed. Verdict unchanged.

One argument in OAuth2TokenService#getAccessToken: the missing-refresh-token MAIL_ACCOUNT_REQUIRES_REAUTH now passes the method's own email parameter as {0} of error.mail.accountRequiresReauth, so the user sees which account to sign in again. The address goes to the local client in detail and messageArgs, as error.account.alreadyExists already does; the fallback message the log gets is unchanged and carries no address. The early return before any provider call, the refresh lock, the permanent/transient split and who sets and clears requires_reauth are untouched. Verdict unchanged.

#886. src-tauri/src gains new_mail.rs, a Windows notification for new mail through tauri-plugin-notification 2.8, driven from Rust only: capabilities/default.json and tauri.conf.json are unchanged, so the page gets none of the plugin's commands. The new command notify_new_mail takes a title and a body, shows the toast only while the main window is hidden, minimized or unfocused, and returns a boolean; a click handler registered at setup calls tray::show_main_window. lib.rs registers the plugin, the command and the handler; tray.rs changes doc comments only. Nothing on the update path moved: no updater command, state, endpoint, pubkey, signature check, download or install step, and not the startup-check preference. Verdict unchanged.

#887. One expression in AboutSettings.svelte, outside its update section: the 'last sync' line of the connection block reads the SSE event's arrivedMessagesCount instead of newMessagesCount, with a comment saying so. The audit cites this file for the manual update check and its failure UI (checkForUpdateManually, RELEASES_URL), the channel switch and the startup-check toggle; none of those lines, their handlers or the imports they use changed. Verdict unchanged.

#890, the v0.2.0-beta.4 cut. The one change in tauri.conf.json since the audited 721bc6e is the top-level version, 0.2.0-beta.3 to 0.2.0-beta.4, written by bump:version (git diff v0.2.0-beta.3 shows that line alone). plugins.updater (endpoints, pubkey 068F68E532BCF6DC) and bundle (the NSIS template, installMode) are untouched. No claim of the audit rests on the value: the build gate compares the tag with this field, the version pin compares the manifest with the version the prompt named, and beta.4 orders after beta.3 and before 0.2.0 under semver, which is the order the beta channel and the later promotion need. Verdict unchanged.

#897, the v0.2.0 cut. The one change in tauri.conf.json since #890 is the top-level version, 0.2.0-beta.4 to 0.2.0, written by bump:version (git diff v0.2.0-beta.4 shows that line alone). plugins.updater (endpoints, pubkey 068F68E532BCF6DC) and bundle are untouched. No claim of the audit rests on the value: the build gate compares the tag with this field, and 0.2.0 orders after every 0.2.0 beta under semver, so the stable redirect serves it and beta.2 to beta.4 installs on the beta channel take it through the updater. Verdict unchanged.

WCAG 2.2 AA fixes, display only. updates.ts: showUpdateFailure takes the dialog text from diagnosticErrorText (the error's own text, `en` when nothing localized it) and stores its language as messageLang; checkForUpdateManually's `message`, which nothing displays, comes from technicalMessage: the error's raw text, as toErrorMessage returned it before this change. UpdateFailureDialog.svelte renders that text with `lang`. BootErrorView.svelte takes an optional errorLang for its error paragraph. AboutSettings.svelte shows the session error through diagnosticErrorText with its `lang`. When an update is checked, which endpoint and channel are asked, how the download is verified against the pubkey and how it is installed are untouched, as are the releases-page fallback and the update channel setting. Verdict unchanged.
